confusions: Parse prints rule warnings for CONF-011 and CONF-012 that every field name is on no table in this branch. Without a workspace I cannot tell whether that is expected or a sign the names are wrong. The skill does not say whether to accept these warnings.
Skill says a policy in a new file should be active=true advisory, but does not say how the tags vocabulary interacts with a new tag like pci-dss.

For 'can't be stored raw' the catalogue has no check that rejects a raw value; the closest, CONF-011, only marks fields sensitive. The skill does not say how to report this gap in the policy statement beyond saying it is not checked.
LOG-001 template limits say to add datadog.log 'with its message and attributes', but the param for attributes is not shown in the catalogue, so only message is covered.
The skill's template list does not say whether to use the template key when the policy covers a broader ask than the template (PCI rather than generic logging).
wished_for: A PCI DSS or payment-data template covering logs, storage, and vendors together
A way to list the datadog.log params fully in the catalogue
Guidance on whether to keep a template key when the request is broader than the template
An example of a rule that uses sensitive or tag scoping for card data
why_confidence: Logging and vendor allowlist rules are direct matches. Storage is only covered by a sensitive marking, not by any check that prevents raw storage. Field names and vendor hosts are guesses, and the PCI audit outcome needs controls no policy can verify.
